hero.title: Precision immune-specificity mapping for human disease.
hero.subtitle: Lab of immune-specificity mapping
hero.description: We map T-cell antigen specificity in patient samples using genetic screens, single-cell profiling, and synthetic biology. Our goal is to uncover mechanisms in autoimmunity, cancer, and infection, then translate them into next-generation targeted therapies.

research_previews.title: Antigen discovery for immune tolerance and autoimmunity
research_previews.text: We integrate cohort immunology, epitope mapping, and spatial tissue profiling to define disease-driving antigens and tolerance opportunities, including a major research program on autoimmune arthritis in pediatric and adult cohorts.

research_previews.title: Functional genomic screens to map immune ligands
research_previews.text: Our lab uses pooled CRISPR perturbation, single-cell phenotyping, and orthogonal validation assays to identify ligand systems that regulate immune activation, persistence, and dysfunction.

research_previews.title: TCR discovery and engineering (αβ and γδ) for cancer translation
research_previews.text: We discover naturally primed αβ and γδ TCRs and engineer receptor formats for translational oncology programs with strong specificity, safety, and developability profiles.
